talks.title: The Science and Magic of Accent Acquisition
talks.speaker: Miranda Guettlein

questions.question: The talk argues that performing a convincing accent is best understood as which of the following?
options: An inborn talent you either have or you don't
A learnable skill with predictable rules and practicable techniques
A purely genetic trait tied to your first language
Random mimicry that can't really be taught
questions.funFact: Dialect coaches routinely teach actors to master a new accent from scratch in a matter of weeks — strong evidence that 'having an ear' is mostly trained, not born.

questions.question: In linguistics, what is the smallest unit of sound that can change the meaning of a word?
questions.funFact: English has about 44 phonemes but only 26 letters — which is exactly why English spelling and pronunciation argue with each other so often.

questions.question: Accent coaches focus on the habitual resting position of the tongue, jaw, and lips that gives a speaker's whole sound its flavor. What is this often called?
questions.funFact: Shift your oral posture — where your tongue habitually rests — and dozens of individual sounds move at once, which is why it's often a coach's very first target.

talks.title: Psychobiotics & The Microbiomes That Make Us
talks.speaker: Ryan Burns

questions.question: Roughly how much does the human gut microbiome weigh, according to the talk?
options: About as much as your brain
About as much as your entire skeleton
questions.funFact: Your gut hosts trillions of microbes weighing on the order of 1.5 kg — comparable to the mass of the human brain.

questions.question: Serotonin is a key mood-related chemical. Where is the large majority of the body's serotonin actually produced?
questions.funFact: Roughly 90% of the body's serotonin is made in the gut — a major reason researchers believe gut microbes can sway mood through the Gut-Brain Axis.

questions.question: The term 'psychobiotic' was coined around 2013 by neuroscientists John Cryan and Ted Dinan. What did their original definition require the microbe to do?
options: Produce a health benefit in people with psychiatric illness
questions.funFact: Their narrow 2013 definition — 'a live organism that, when ingested in adequate amounts, produces a health benefit in patients suffering from psychiatric illness' — has broadened a lot since.

questions.question: In what city did the very first Nerd Nite take place?
questions.funFact: The very first Nerd Nite happened at Boston's Midway Cafe back in 2003.

questions.question: What is Nerd Nite's official motto?
questions.funFact: "Be there and be square" has been the Nerd Nite tagline from the early days — nerdiness worn as a badge of honor.

questions.question: Nerd Nite began because grad student Chris Balakrishnan kept retelling bar stories about his fieldwork. What was he studying?
questions.funFact: Balakrishnan studied brood-parasitic indigobirds in Cameroon; his bartenders got so tired of the repeat stories they told him to just give a proper talk.

originStory.text:
Welcome to Nerdometer.

Here's how it works: three rounds, one for each of tonight's topics. Questions get harder — and worth more — as you go. Answer on your phone. The leaderboard is live.

Be there and be square. Let's play.

A little history.

Nerd Nite started in Boston in 2003. A grad student named Chris Balakrishnan kept telling the same stories at his local bar — about studying parasitic birds in Cameroon. The bartenders finally said: just give a talk. He did. People came.

Twenty years later it's in over 100 cities on six continents — and one of them is right here in Fort Collins.

Why we do this:

Fort Collins deserves a place where curious people gather, learn something strange, and talk to a stranger about it over a beer. That's the whole idea. Thanks for being here and making it real.

Trivia's done — but you're not done yet.
